parallel.requirements: Recognized the need to implement a complete Pylama package with setup files, multiple linters, config support, scanning, formatting, async execution, and hooks.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Worked as a single parent actor despite parallel mode: no Task, Workflow, Agent, or child-log activity was present, and all exploration and implementation ownership stayed with the main agent.
parallel.implementation: Downloaded and cloned upstream Pylama, copied the reference source into /workspace, ran tests, and investigated failures around pylint confidence, context, lint loading, pytest, and core modules.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Delivered a copied upstream-style workspace but did not complete or submit a fixed final implementation before timeout; final response was empty.
parallel.verification: Ran a baseline pytest command that reported two failures and 33 passing tests, then investigated the failures without a subsequent passing local run in the projected evidence.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation completed at 32 of 34 tests, so two evaluator cases remained unsatisfied; no concurrency mechanism was involved in the failure.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Pylama obligations and additionally focused on compatibility details for installed plugin APIs, entry points, unified exports, error aliases, hooks, and option handling.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Worked sequentially as one actor, with no child agents; the same actor owned investigation, implementation edits, local testing, and final workspace state.
serial.implementation: Copied upstream develop sources and made edits to inirama parsing, linter discovery, setup.cfg, dummy.py, __init__.py exports, Error behavior, RunContext, main.check_paths, hooks, and linter classes.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Integrated all changes directly in the shared workspace as a single actor and left an artifact containing the expected package and tests, but the run ended by timeout without a final response.
serial.verification: Ran local upstream tests repeatedly, moved from a failing baseline to 35 passing local tests, and performed small import and API smoke checks.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite stronger local verification, official evaluation still completed at 32 of 34 tests, indicating remaining hidden-task gaps rather than a serial-control or delegation issue.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel-mode attempt received the complete Pylama requirements and started from upstream Pylama plus official tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial attempt received the same prompt and recognized extra compatibility obligations such as plugin entry points and unified API exports.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had the same stated task, but the serial run acted on more of the prompt-specific API requirements while the parallel run stopped at investigation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run used a single main actor and no child-task decomposition, despite being run in parallel mode.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run also used a single actor, with workflows and delegation tools disabled in the command line.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no multi-agent ownership contrast; the difference is that serial continued through implementation edits while parallel did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: No child briefs, handoffs, or cross-agent contracts existed; the agent inspected upstream source and external linter behavior directly.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: No child briefs or handoffs existed; the agent personally inspected plugin entry points, linter APIs, and compatibility constraints before editing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial gathered and used more interface context locally, but no context crossed an agent boundary in either trajectory.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run copied upstream Pylama 8.4.1 into the workspace and investigated but did not perform implementation edits in the projected semantic timeline.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run copied upstream develop and made concrete edits across configuration, linter registration, dummy.py, public API exports, errors, context, main, and hooks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial produced a substantially modified artifact, while parallel largely delivered the upstream reference state with unresolved baseline failures.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: There were no child results to retrieve or join; the only lifecycle issue was that the main process reached timeout after investigation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results; serial changes were made directly by the same actor and the run also ended by timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No result lifecycle coordination difference exists; both terminal states were timeout-driven, with serial having more local work completed before timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workspace was modified by one actor copying the upstream tree; protocol validation recorded no workflow child logs or delegation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial workspace was edited by one actor through direct Edit and Write operations, also with no delegation or child logs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no shared-state race or merge issue; serial simply performed more single-actor edits before evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel local testing reported a failing baseline with two failures and 33 passing tests, and official evaluation later reported 32 of 34.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial local testing eventually reported 35 passing upstream tests, but official evaluation still reported 32 of 34.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had stronger local acceptance evidence, yet it did not translate to a passing official score; this is an ordinary verification coverage gap, not a coordination failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel-mode process used the full 2399-second budget, returned code 143, and had an empty final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial process also used the full 2399-second budget, returned code 143, and had an empty final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both closed under timeout; serial consumed more requests and tool calls while completing more implementation work, but neither reached a passing official artifact.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is both_fail, not discordant: both current status records completed evaluation with 32 passed, 2 failed, 34 total, and solution_passed false. The parallel-mode run did not use parallelism and stopped after copying and investigating upstream code, while the serial run implemented and locally verified more changes but still missed two official evaluator cases. The task-solving difference is implementation depth and local-test coverage, not a concurrency-specific episode.
parallel_contributors: Parallel-mode trajectory copied upstream Pylama and investigated baseline failures but did not make projected implementation edits before timeout.
Protocol validation reports no delegation or child-agent activity, so no parallel coordination mechanism contributed to the final score.
serial_contributors: Serial trajectory made concrete compatibility edits and got local upstream tests passing.
Serial official evaluation still failed two of thirty-four cases, so local tests did not cover all required behavior.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial changed more files and APIs than parallel, including __init__.py exports, Error compatibility, RunContext, check_paths, setup.cfg, hooks, and linter loading.
Parallel left copied upstream source closer to its original state and did not finish the same prompt-specific adaptations.
evaluator_effects: Only aggregate official counts are included under /pair, so the two failed evaluator cases cannot be identified from current pair-local evidence.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported process contrast only
